problems.q: A gas sample is at 1520 mmHg. What is that pressure in atm? Use 760 mmHg = 1 atm.
problems.why: 1520 mmHg / 760 mmHg per atm = 2.00 atm. OpenStax AF2e §8.1.
hints: Divide by 760. A larger mmHg reading means more than 1 atm.

problems.q: A gas sample occupies 1.50 L at 27 °C. The pressure stays the same and the temperature becomes 127 °C. What is the new volume? Convert each temperature with K = °C + 273.
problems.why: Charles’s law needs kelvin: 27 + 273 = 300 K and 127 + 273 = 400 K. V2 = 1.50 L × (400 K / 300 K) = 2.00 L. OpenStax AF2e §8.2.
hints: Do not put 27 and 127 straight into the ratio. Add 273 to each Celsius temperature first.
